misconceptions.description: Treating a list of named modules or theories as synthesis, instead of letting the lenses jointly shape one decision
misconceptions.trigger: the tension map cites TPACK, equity, and ethics but no lens changes the final decision
misconceptions.feedback: Show how each module lens altered the negotiated decision. If naming a module changes nothing, it is a citation, not synthesis.

misconceptions.description: Naming two competing classroom values but never stating how the collision was resolved
misconceptions.trigger: the map lists efficiency and equity side by side with no priority rule or rationale
misconceptions.feedback: State the priority rule you used when the values collided and the classroom evidence that justified it.

misconceptions.description: Letting the AI decide which classroom value should win the tension rather than surfacing options for the teacher to judge
misconceptions.trigger: learner adopts the model's chosen value without an evidence check or recorded reason
misconceptions.feedback: Use AI to widen the values you consider, then make the negotiated call yourself and record why.

misconceptions.description: Assuming one prescribed decision is correct regardless of context, rather than judging the reasoning across lenses
misconceptions.trigger: learner scores a map only by whether it matches the answer key
misconceptions.feedback: Judge the map on whether the cross-module reasoning fits this classroom, not on matching one outcome.
